chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure.' He said:
If a thief steals in other than Makkah, or commits a felony upon himself, and flees to Makkah, he is not seized for as long as he remains in the Sanctuary (Al-Haram), until he exits from it.
But he is prevented from the market, and he is neither bought from nor sat with, until he exits from it, at which point he is seized.
And if he commits that same crime inside the Sanctuary, he is seized inside it.

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca), a sacred area with specific legal protections
key_terms.يُبَايَعُ: To buy/sell or conduct business transactions

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a criminal seeking refuge in Mecca according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential nuance of 'aman' (security) in Mecca, distinguishing between physical immunity from immediate arrest and the restriction of civil liberties, such as market access and social interaction. It establishes that while a fugitive is protected from being seized within the Haram boundaries, they remain liable for their crime and are effectively under house arrest until they depart, unless the offense occurs within the Sanctuary itself. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of Mecca as a zone of temporary sanctuary rather than absolute impunity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:97] and whoever enters it shall be secure. Heasws said: ‘

If a thief were to steal in other than Makkah or commits a felony (offence) upon himself, so he flees to Makkah, he would not be seized for as long as he in inside the Al-Harram, until he comes out from it.
But he can be prevented from the market, and he can neither sell, nor sat with, until he comes out from it, and he would be seized.
And, if he was to do (a crime) inside the Al-Harram that which he did, he would be seized inside it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of the words of Allah, ‘Whoever enters it he gains immunity.

5 [3:96] He (the Imam) said, ‘If a thief steals something in a place other than Makkah or commits a crime against his own self, then flees to Makkah, he cannot be arrested in al-Haram (the sacred area) until he comes out. However, he can be stopped from going to the market places, selling, buying and from sitting with people until he goes out of al-Haram (the sacred area), then he can be arrested, but if he commits such things inside al-Haram (the sacred area) he can be arrested and taken in custody. ‘“
